Note::dedent¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::dedent() const

Remove The Common Leading Indentation From Every Line¶

dedent() returns a new Note, same shape as the input, with the largest run of leading whitespace that every non-blank line shares removed from each line of a cell. It is the standard fix for text captured from an indented source block — a here-doc, a code snippet, a quoted paragraph — so the content starts at column zero without disturbing its internal structure.

Lines are split on \n. Only whitespace (spaces and tabs) counts as indentation, and only the common amount is stripped: a line indented more than the others keeps the extra. Blank lines are ignored when measuring the common indent. If the lines share no leading whitespace, the cell is returned unchanged.

dedent operates within each cell and does not merge or reflow lines. It is shape-preserving, cell-independent, and returns a fresh Note.

Example 1: A Batch¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::make_note({"    line1\n    line2\n      line3", "no indent"}).dedent())
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["line1\nline2\n  line3", "no indent"]

Four spaces — the common indent — are removed from every line; "line3", indented six, keeps the extra two. The second cell has no shared indent and is unchanged.

See Also¶

  • Note::indent: the inverse — add a fixed indent to every line.

  • Note::strip: trim the whole cell’s edges rather than each line’s.

  • Note::split_lines: work with the lines individually.
